item.text:
**4B.8 Research Note**

Overall, the 2024 record is negative. Putin completed the formal inauguration and term start, but the available evidence shows that term limits had already been rewritten to keep him eligible through 2036, the 2024 election lacked genuine competition, and there is no credible sign of a real constitutional transfer of power or coalition-based succession.

| Direction | Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable URL | Claim-level summary | IDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| Weak pro | [Putin formally begins new six-year term](https://en.kremlin.ru/events/president/news/73981) | President of Russia | 2024-05-07 | https://en.kremlin.ru/events/president/news/73981 | The Kremlin recorded the formal start of Putin’s new six-year term. This shows procedural continuity and formal compliance with the inauguration ritual, but not respect for genuine succession rules or meaningful transfer of power. | `4B.8` |
| Against | [Russia: Freedom in the World 2024](https://freedomhouse.org/country/russia/freedom-world/2024) | Freedom House | 2024 | https://freedomhouse.org/country/russia/freedom-world/2024 | Freedom House says 2020 constitutional amendments let Putin, but not future presidents, run for two more terms, potentially keeping him in office until 2036. It also says Russia has never had a democratic transfer of power between rival groups. | `4B.8`, `4B.1`, `4B.2`, `4B.4`, `4B.5` |
| Against | [Russia: Nations in Transit 2024](https://freedomhouse.org/country/russia/nations-transit/2024) | Freedom House | 2024 | https://freedomhouse.org/country/russia/nations-transit/2024 | Freedom House says Putin and his allies effectively control parliament, the legislature is not freely elected, and political centralization has increased at the expense of regional autonomy. That is evidence against coalition commitments and against a genuine constitutional transfer. | `4B.8`, `4B.2`, `4B.4`, `4B.5` |

That is direct evidence against a meaningful constitutional transfer of power. | `4B.8`, `4B.1`, `4B.2`, `4B.5` |

**Assessment**

- I found no credible 2024 evidence that Putin respected term limits as a binding constraint, upheld succession competition, or accepted a real transfer of power.
- The only pro-looking evidence is the formal inauguration on May 7, 2024, which shows ceremony, not genuine alternation.
- Coalition commitments are effectively absent from the record; I found no 2024 evidence of power-sharing or restraint that would let an opposing bloc replace the ruling circle through constitutional means.

**Search gap**

- I did not find any credible 2024 source showing Putin prepared to cede power, observe term limits as a real constraint, or permit a meaningful succession process. The evidence points instead to a managed system designed to preserve continuity through formal procedure without real contestability.
